case1_simple_assignment.py.notes: No SQL sinks present. Pure safe code.

case2_sqli_concatenation.py.notes: Classic SQLi: user input concatenated directly into SQL string.

case3_sqli_fstring.py.notes: Flask request parameter interpolated via f-string into SQL.

case4_sqli_printf.py.notes: HTTP form data injected via Python % string formatting.

case5_safe_sanitizer.py.notes: int() converts tainted input to integer, breaking string taint chain. str(safe_id) produces a safe string.

expected_vulnerabilities.notes: user_input (implicit external) → += concatenation → execute(base_query). Conditional path.

case6_augassign_conditional.py.notes: Taint enters via undefined variable user_input, propagates through augmented assignment.

case7_orm_injection.py.notes: Two user inputs (username, limit) flow into f-string query.

case8_safe_orm.py.notes: Uses SQLAlchemy text() with parameter binding via dict. Tainted values (username, search_term, product_id) are passed as parameters (second argument to execute), NOT interpolated into the SQL string. The SQL string itself contains only placeholders (:username, :limit, :search, etc.).

expected_vulnerabilities.notes: input() → replace/strip (not sanitizers) → f-string → concatenation → execute(final_query). replace() and strip() are NOT SQL sanitizers.
Multiple input() calls → concatenation → execute(query). username is partially sanitized (replace) but email and bio are fully tainted.

case9_complex_propagation.py.notes: Taint flows through replace(), split(), join(), f-strings. replace() is NOT a SQL sanitizer.

expected_vulnerabilities.notes: Three input() calls → string concatenation → execute(sql). Column, table, and value all tainted.
Three more input() calls → augmented assignment concatenation → execute(base_sql).

case10_dynamic_columns.py.notes: Dynamic SQL construction with user-controlled table/column names.

case11_enterprise_app.py.notes: All queries use parameterized form (? placeholders). Input goes through sanitize_search_term() and int() before use. Table/column names validated against allowlists. Tainted values passed as parameters tuple (second arg to execute), not interpolated into SQL strings.
